**Question:** Which character encoding should the tool use when reading and writing log text? (FR-005)

**Why it matters:** If the tool follows whatever encoding the user's machine happens to be configured for, the same log file can produce different output on two machines — and the "undecodable bytes pass through unchanged" promise becomes untestable. Fixing one encoding makes output reproducible everywhere.

**Recommended:** Option A — a fixed UTF-8 decode with byte-preserving error handling is the only choice that satisfies both the spec's "byte-for-byte unchanged" guarantee and the constitution's "no hidden state" constraint (behaviour must not depend on ambient environment), while still using nothing beyond the standard library.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Always UTF-8 for both input and output, with undecodable bytes preserved exactly and round-tripped (never replaced or dropped), regardless of locale or environment variables |
| B | Follow the platform/locale default encoding, as Python normally does for files and streams |
| C | Treat input as raw bytes throughout and never decode at all; match and replace on bytes |
| D | Always UTF-8, but abort with a diagnostic and non-zero exit on the first undecodable byte |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
